title: GACED30: Global 30-m Annual Cropland Extent Dynamics (2000–2024)
description: Annual 30 m global cropland extent maps for each year from 2000 to 2024, generated from the gap-free Global 30-m Seamless Data Cube (SDC30) with year-specific classifiers. Each tile is a 25-band GeoTIFF (one band per year) with cropland / non-cropland classes. The authors describe it as the first dedicated global 30 m annual cropland-extent dataset.
purpose: Offers an annual (rather than multi-year epoch) cropland time series at 30 m for 25 years, allowing year-to-year cropland dynamics, cropping frequency and expansion of irrigated perimeters in Algeria to be examined against national statistics.

references.citation: Liao, Y., Chen, S., Bai, Y., Wang, J., and Gong, P. (2026) Global 30 m annual cropland extent dynamics (2000–2024): a harmonized baseline of structural evolution and regional disparities. Earth System Science Data, 18, 7071–7096.

spatial_extent.description: Global land surface in non-overlapping 3° × 3° tiles, packaged on Zenodo in 60 ZIP files each spanning 6° of longitude. Algeria (about 9°W–12°E) falls in the lon_-012_to_-006, lon_-006_to_+000, lon_+000_to_+006 and lon_+006_to_+012 packages; users must mosaic and clip Algeria themselves.

format: GeoTIFF (Cloud Optimized), 25 bands per tile, in ZIP packages

variables.name: Cropland extent (bands 1–25, years 2000–2024)
variables.description: 0 = non-cropland; 10 = cropland (active annual crops, perennial woody crops, active fallow and agricultural structures such as greenhouses); 255 = NoData.

processing: Daily gap-free surface reflectance from the Global 30 m Seamless Data Cube (SDC30) was aggregated into 8-day median composites and combined with spectral indices (e.g. NDVI, kNDVI, MNDWI, tasseled cap) and NASADEM terrain and location features. Year-specific CatBoost classifiers were trained using the expert-annotated FAST sample set plus spatially augmented samples (screened for label noise), followed by rule-based spatial and temporal refinement. The annual record was used to derive cropping frequency and 1 km structural-evolution indicators described in the paper.
validation: Liao et al. (2026, ESSD) report, against independent stable-site FAST-Crop samples, an overall accuracy of 0.965 and an F1 score of 0.844; in a matched regional assessment in China, OA 0.946 and F1 0.840. National cropland areas agreed with definition-reconciled FAOSTAT statistics with R² = 0.95 and an area-weighted direction match rate of 83.1%. The authors note that absolute crop gain/loss transition scores remained modest.
limitations: Recently published (ESSD, September 2026); independent evaluation by other groups, particularly in North Africa, is not yet available. The paper gives no accuracy figures specific to North Africa or Algeria.
The authors report spectral confusion between active fallow and natural bare land, and larger map discrepancies in semi-arid and transitional regions.

Cropland includes perennial woody crops, active fallow and greenhouses but excludes temporary meadows and pastures, so totals differ by definition from GLAD (no woody crops) and WorldCereal temporary crops.
Intermediate cropping frequencies reported in some drylands may reflect rotation, fallow or classification variability rather than true cultivation changes.

algeria_notes: Because GACED30 counts active fallow and perennial woody crops (olive groves, date palms) as cropland, Algerian totals are expected to be higher than products restricted to annual or herbaceous crops; the reported fallow-versus-bare-land confusion is a particular concern in the semi-arid High Plateaus and steppe margins. The annual series is well suited to tracking the growth of centre-pivot and other irrigated perimeters in the Sahara, but users should check isolated pixels in the desert before interpreting them as cultivation.
